name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 23 points
Joyce holds an overwhelming cash advantage over Farnham
No polls or expert ratings indicate competition
model.rationale: The district's 23-point Republican lean, Joyce's roughly 70-to-1 financial advantage, and market pricing near 96% Republican leave no evidence of a competitive race, so the forecast stays at Safe Republican.
model.watch: Any independent polling or meaningful outside spending backing Farnham would be the first sign of competition in this seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-13 covers south-central Pennsylvania and leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. John Joyce, the incumbent Republican, is running for another term after securing his party's nomination. No general-election polls or expert ratings exist for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals.

The financial picture is lopsided: Joyce has raised about $2.4 million and holds $3.8 million on hand, while Democrat Beth Farnham has raised roughly $55,000 with about $16,000 available. Prediction markets give Joyce about a 96% chance of winning. With no outside spending or independent polling suggesting competition, the seat is rated Safe for Republicans, and an upset would require a dramatic, unforeseen shift in the district's politics.
